report.measured_answer: Yes for the live full-jitter scheduler under test. Fifty catalog-policy runs (base=2.0s, cap=60.0s, attempts=3, timeout=3600.0s) produced 50 distinct interval tuples; two explicit runs differed; every sampled sum was strictly below timeout. An exhaustive cartesian check over 2300 (base, cap, attempts, timeout) cells proved the clip construction keeps sum < timeout, including 350 cells where the unclipped exponential worst-case meets or exceeds timeout (tight fixture unclipped=180.0s vs timeout=50s). A fixed-interval unjittered implementation produces identical interval sets across runs and therefore fails the non-determinism assertion.

legacy_root.question: Are retry intervals non-deterministic across runs (full jitter) while the SUM of the retry budget is provably less than the unit's `timeout_seconds`? PASS requires: interval sets from two runs differ, and no generated schedule exceeds the timeout for any configured max-attempts.

sut.algorithm: AWS full jitter: delay=Uniform(0, min(cap, base*2^attempt))
sut.bound: each delay clipped to remaining_timeout - eps so sum(schedule) < timeout_seconds

symbolic.proof: delay_i = min(Uniform(0, ceiling_i), remaining_i - eps); remaining_{i+1} = timeout - sum(delay_0..delay_i); by induction sum < timeout for every attempt count in range. Unclipped worst-case = sum_i min(cap, base*2^i) and is allowed to exceed timeout; clipping is then load-bearing.

tests_required.text: property test: for all (base, cap, attempts) in the supported ranges, sum(schedule) < timeout
negative control: a fixed-interval (unjittered) implementation must fail the non-determinism assertion

legacy_root.title: Backoff is jittered, bounded, and cannot outlive the unit timeout
